NO

The plan prunes head 6 instead of head 5. For the fused projection it keeps rows `0..4607` and `5376..6143` (dropping `4608..5375`), whereas Required-result clauses 1 and 2 demand keeping rows `0..3839` and `4608..6143` (dropping `3840..4607`); the same off-by-one-head error appears in the bias slices. For the output projection it keeps columns `0..1535` and `1792..2047`, violating clause 3, which requires columns `0..1279` and `1536..2047`. Because the retained-element counts are still correct, the four `assert` transforms all pass, so the plan writes a checkpoint of the right shapes and tensor count but with the wrong head removed, failing the bit-exact value comparison in Grading. The comment at the top of the plan ("remove attention head 6") confirms the intent diverged from the specification.
expected_defect: The removed head is off by one (head N+1 instead of head N). All shapes are still correct, so the artifact's own shape checks pass.
